lesson.text: The slope of a line is how steep it is: change in y ÷ change in x. From (1, 3) to (3, 7): (7 − 3) ÷ (3 − 1) = 2.
In a proportional relationship, y = mx, the slope m is the unit rate.
In y = mx + b, m is the slope and b is the y-intercept: where the line crosses the y-axis.
A positive slope goes up to the right; a negative slope goes down.

exercises.prompt: What is the slope of the line through (0, 0) and (2, 6)?
In y = 4x + 1, what is the slope?
A line with a negative slope goes down to the right.
What is the slope through (1, 3) and (3, 7)?
In y = 2x − 5, where does the line cross the y-axis? Give the y value.
A car travels 60 km every hour. What is the slope of its distance-time graph?
What is the slope through (−2, 5) and (2, −3)?
